summary: Defines Asynchronous Layered Coding (ALC), a protocol for sending files reliably from one sender to a very large number of receivers at once, such as over multicast or broadcast. It combines layered coding transport, congestion control and forward error correction building blocks. It is a proposed standard that replaced RFC 3450.

eli5.summary: A teacher reads a story over a loudspeaker to a huge crowd, adding extra repeated clues so anyone who misses a word can still piece it together without asking.

questions: how to deliver files to many receivers with multicast
how does alc deliver files over multicast
what is the alc source packet indicator
subtitle: Reliable file delivery to a huge audience over multicast, with no feedback from receivers at all.

tldr.problem: Delivering the same content reliably to potentially millions of receivers is hard if every receiver must report back to the sender.
tldr.mechanism: ALC sends FEC-encoded packets over IP multicast on several channels. Receivers adjust their own rate by joining and leaving channels, and simply wait until enough packets arrive to rebuild the object.
tldr.outcome: The sender's load is the same for one receiver or a million. This Proposed Standard obsoletes the Experimental RFC 3450.

today: RFC 5775 is a Proposed Standard published in April 2010. It obsoletes the Experimental RFC 3450, and the metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Goals and Scalability
sections.content:
Asynchronous Layered Coding (ALC) is a content delivery protocol designed for massive scalability on top of IP multicast. In this context the RFC means potentially millions of concurrent receivers, aggregate object sizes from hundreds of kilobytes to hundreds of gigabytes, receivers that each start asynchronously, and all of it from a single sender.

ALC keeps the scalability of multicast while adding what plain multicast lacks: session management, congestion control and reliability. To each receiver it looks like a dedicated session whose rate adapts to congestion on its path. To the sender there is no difference in load or outgoing rate whether one or a million receivers have joined. No feedback packets are required from receivers.

ALC is deliberately minimal. It leaves out application-specific features that could limit scalability, and it says that how receivers learn the session description, or report statistics, is out of scope.
sections.eli5: ALC is like a radio station. The station sends the same thing no matter how many people tune in, and listeners never have to call in.

sections.title: Three Building Blocks
sections.content:
ALC is assembled from three existing building blocks. Layered Coding Transport (LCT, RFC 5651) provides in-band session management. A multiple rate congestion control building block provides feedback-free congestion control, and implementations must at least support the one in RFC 3738. The FEC building block (RFC 5052) provides reliability.

The sender spreads encoding symbols for an object across several channels at different rates. Each receiver joins and leaves channels to match the bandwidth between it and the sender, independently of other receivers. Receivers do not ask for retransmission of individual packets. They wait for enough packets to reconstruct the object, so the sender's packets and rate do not depend on how many receivers there are.

An ALC session consists of multiple channels from a single sender, carrying packets for one or more objects. Congestion control applies to the aggregate of the channels in the session. This document defines version 1 of ALC, which must use version 1 of LCT, and carries ALC as the payload of UDP over IP multicast. Together with RFC 5651, RFC 5052 and RFC 3738, it is said to completely specify a working reliable multicast transport protocol that conforms to RFC 2357.
sections.eli5: ALC snaps together three LEGO parts: one tags the pieces, one controls how fast to send, and one adds spare clues so lost pieces can be rebuilt.

sections.title: Packet Format and Sessions
sections.content:
An ALC packet is an IP packet (IPv4 or IPv6) followed by a UDP header, an LCT header, a FEC Payload ID and then the encoding symbols. The Congestion Control Information (CCI) field inside the LCT header carries data for the congestion control block. The CCI length must be one of 32, 64, 96 or 128 bits and stay the same for every packet in a session.

Each session has a Transport Session Identifier (TSI), carried in every packet. The pair of sender IP address and TSI must uniquely identify the session. If a session carries more than one object, the Transmission Object Identifier (TOI) must be used to say which object a packet belongs to. With a single object, the TOI may be omitted.

Two bits in the LCT header are the Protocol Specific Indication. The first is the Source Packet Indicator, set to 1 for packets that carry only source data when a systematic FEC scheme has separate payload id formats for source and repair packets. The second is reserved. Packets with no payload may be sent, for example to signal the end of a session. This document also defines a new LCT header extension, EXT_FTI (type 64), to carry FEC Object Transmission Information in-band.
sections.eli5: Each packet has a label saying which broadcast it belongs to and which object it is a piece of, so receivers can sort the pieces into the right piles.

sections.title: Session Description and Receiver Steps
sections.content:
Before joining, a receiver needs a Session Description. It includes which congestion control block is used, the sender IP address, the number of channels, the address and port of each channel, the TSI, whether the session carries more than one object, and any header extension formats. How the description reaches receivers is outside the RFC, which lists SDP, XML metadata, HTTP/MIME headers or a session announcement protocol as examples.

For every packet it gets, a receiver follows a fixed order. It must check the header is valid, and discard the packet if not. It must check that the sender address and TSI match a session it joined, or silently discard. It must act on the CCI field according to the congestion control block. With several objects, it must check the TOI is valid. It should then use the FEC Payload ID and the symbols to rebuild the object.

The sender must use the same TSI for all packets in a session, give each object a unique TOI when it sends more than one, and send at the rates the congestion control block dictates.
sections.eli5: When a packet arrives, the receiver asks: is it formatted right, is it from the show I tuned into, and which object is it for? Only then does it use the packet.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC calls ALC especially vulnerable to denial of service from forged packets, partly because many receivers may receive the same forged packet. A single forged packet used in reconstruction can make the whole object come out wrong. It recommends protection at two levels.

At the application level, receivers should check the integrity of the whole object once rebuilt, ideally with a digital signature, and discard it if the check fails. At the packet level, it recommends packet authentication so that forged packets are dropped individually and the damage is proportional to the number of forged packets, not the object size. RFC 5776 (TESLA) and a simple authentication draft are named as suitable schemes. Authentication also helps against forged congestion control information.

Reverse Path Forwarding checks should be enabled on routers and switches along the path. The RFC also describes a baseline mode using IPsec ESP in transport mode for secure single-sender operation, with automated key management recommended.
sections.eli5: If a prankster slips fake puzzle pieces into the crowd, everyone's picture comes out wrong. So listeners should check each piece is genuine and check the finished picture.

sections.title: What Changed from RFC 3450
sections.content:
This document moves the protocol from the Experimental category of RFC 3450 to the Standards Track. It stays backwards compatible with RFC 3450, updated for accumulated experience.

The changes include removing the Statement of Intent and the Intellectual Property section, removing material duplicated in LCT, splitting normative and informative references, and aligning with new versions of the LCT and FEC building blocks. It also defines the Source Packet Indicator in the Protocol Specific Indication bits, and defines and registers the EXT_FTI header extension, with IANA value 64.
sections.eli5: The first trial version was tidied up and made official, with one new label added so receivers that skip the repair math can still use plain pieces.
